faroConnectButton.noPasswordIsSentYouReview: No password is sent. You review and connect in Faro.
faroConnectButton.noReachableHostForThisItem: No reachable host for this item yet, so Faro connect is unavailable.

revoke.title: Revoke "{{name}}"?
revoke.message: The link stops working and the key is removed from every server it was installed on. Faro connections using it start failing right away.
revoke.partial: Revoked, but the key could not be removed from {{count}} server(s) yet. It will keep retrying.

page.title: Access
page.subtitle: Give someone time-boxed SSH and SFTP access to your servers with one Faro link. No passwords change hands, and revoking removes the key.

empty.title: No one has access yet
empty.message: Create a link for a teammate or contractor. They open it in Faro, accept, and get SFTP and terminal access to the servers you picked until it ends or you revoke it.

create.failed: Could not create the access link
create.errTooMany: A grant covers at most 64 servers
create.errUsername: Lowercase letters, digits, "_" or "-", up to 32 characters
create.errBridgeIsTarget: The bridge cannot also be one of the granted servers
create.title: New access
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: Who this is for. Faro shows it on the consent screen and uses it as the connection group.
create.noServers: No managed servers yet. Connect a server with the ServerKit agent first.
create.durationHint: The link and the key both stop working then. On OpenSSH 8.2 or newer, sshd also refuses the key at that time even if the panel is unreachable.
create.createUser: Create this user on servers where it doesn't exist
create.rootHint: root gives full control of every granted server. A dedicated user is safer when the person only needs their site.
create.bridgeHint: Faro connects through this server first. It gets the same key, limited to reaching the granted servers on port 22, so every person arrives from one static address.
create.restrictSource: Only accept the key from the bridge
create.restrictSourceHint: Adds from="bridge address" on the granted servers. Leave off if the bridge reaches them over a private network address the panel doesn't know.

retry.success: Done. Every server is up to date.
retry.partial: {{count}} server(s) still failing. See the errors below.

extend.partial: Extended, but {{count}} server(s) kept the old key expiry. Retry from this page.
extend.title: Extend "{{name}}"
extend.intro: Access will end this long from now:

delete.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
delete.message: Removes this record from the list. The key is already gone from every server. The audit log keeps its history.

detail.notFound: This access grant does not exist anymore.
detail.partialTitle: Some servers did not get the key
detail.partialBody: The person can reach the servers marked Installed. Fix the error shown for the others (often an offline agent), then retry.
detail.cleanupTitle: The key is still on some servers
detail.cleanupBody: Access is revoked in the panel, but these servers could not be reached to remove the key. ServerKit retries every 5 minutes for a day; you can retry now.
detail.waitingTitle: Waiting for the person to accept
detail.waitingBody: The link was shown once when you created it. If it was lost, revoke this and create a new one.
detail.sourceLocked: key only accepted from the bridge

link.copyFailed: Copy failed. Select the link and copy it manually.
link.title: Share this link
link.intro: Send this link to the person you are giving access to. They open it with Faro, review the servers, and click Accept.
link.onceBody: Treat it like a password until it is redeemed: whoever opens it first gets the access. It works once and expires {{when}}.
